text:
All fixed. The root cause was in `versions/compare.py`:

1. **`parse` returned raw string components** instead of the ints its docstring promised, so `compare` compared release components lexicographically — `"10" < "9"` and `"02" != "2"`. Fixed by returning `[int(p) for p in parts]`.
2. **`zip_longest` used `fillvalue="0"`** (a string), which would raise `TypeError` once components became ints when comparing versions of different lengths (e.g. `"1.2"` vs `"1.2.0"`). Changed to `fillvalue=0`.

Verified: all three issue cases now behave correctly (`1.10.0 > 1.9.0`, `2.0.0 < 10.0.0`, `1.02.0 == 1.2.0`), and the existing test suite passes.
